disease_label_per_paper: Infectious aortitis: a life-threatening endovascular complication of nontyphoidal Salmonella bacteremia

demographics.ethnicity_or_origin: Japanese man living in the United States

presentation_summary: 65-year-old Japanese man with hypertension and chronic hepatitis B presented with diffuse body aches, spiking pyrexia, chills, lower back pain, and abdominal pain for 5 days.
He denied recent travel, rash, diarrhea, or rectal bleeding; examination was stable except for temperature 38.9 degC.
Labs showed mild leukocytosis/neutrophilia, hyponatremia, elevated AST/ALT, ESR 107 mm/hr, and CRP 17.4 mg/dL.
Abdominal CT showed infrarenal aortitis; multiple blood cultures grew Salmonella enterica serotype Enteritidis with ceftriaxone susceptibility and ciprofloxacin non-susceptibility.

Salmonella enterica serotype Enteritidis was isolated from multiple blood cultures
The antibiotic regimen was switched to IV ceftriaxone 2 g/24 hr
developed progressive abdominal and back pain and persistent pyrexia and mild leukocytosis. Follow-up abdominal CT one week later showed progressive inflammatory changes
underwent surgical resection of the infected aortic segment with in-situ aortoiliac rifampin-impregnated Dacron graft
complete a further 5 week course of IV therapy... planned lifelong antibiotic suppressive therapy with amoxicillin
